subject: Request: full subprocessors inventory + transition plan (audit)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datapulse.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@datapulse.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: full subprocessors inventory + transition plan (audit)

Ben —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. DataPulse has an upcoming vendor audit and SOC2 spot-check on Aug 5 and we need an authoritative picture of Redwood's processing partners before then. Can you provide the following by COB Tue (28 Jul)?

- Current subprocessor roster (names + primary function)
- Country/region where each subprocessor processes customer data
- Role classification (storage, telemetry, logging, analytics, ML infra, support)
- Whether each one has access to customer plaintext or only encrypted metadata
- Any subprocessors added or removed in the last 12 months (and change dates)
- For critical telemetry/logging partners, a short fallback/transition plan in case of deprovisioning (we had a request from our compliance team specifically about vendor attrition)

If you have a single CSV or spreadsheet that's easiest — we can slot it straight into our evidence bundle. Also include any redline/annex language you propose for customers concerned about cross-border routing.

Attaching the questionnaire we usually share for other vendors; feel free to respond in-line or send separate files.

Samir
Samir Patel
Vendor Risk Manager, DataPulse
samir.patel@datapulse.com

Attachment: vendor_questionnaire_template.pdf (1 page)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datapulse.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessors inventory + transition plan (audit)

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. I've pulled the latest inventory and attached two artifacts: a roster export and a high-level dataflow diagram. A few quick notes up front:

- We had a supplier change for our logging/observability provider (EdgeLogix -> LogStreamer) on 2026-05-18; LogStreamer is now the primary telemetry ingest for hosted customers.
- No processors have access to plaintext user content except our storage layer (on customer opt-in) and the secure indexing service (both are documented in the roster).
- We maintain KMS tenancy mappings by customer region; I'll include the KMS region column in the roster export.

Next steps: Kimberly (Legal) will provide any DPA amendment language and Jordan (Infra) can supply the transition/rollback notes for the logging provider. We should be able to get a packaged CSV + dataflow diagram and a draft DPA clause by Mon morning.

If you need an executive sign-off note or a quick call to walk compliance through the artifacts, happy to schedule — I'm available Mon 10:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: roster_20260725.csv (spreadsheet), dataflow_20260725.png (diagram)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datapulse.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessors inventory + transition plan (audit)

Samir / Ben —

Thanks, Ben — I reviewed the roster and dataflow. I attached a redline of the DPA clause we typically offer for customers wanting stricter controls when telemetry or logging partners are involved. A few items for compliance to note: 

- We will flag processors that are used for support/ops only vs. production inference. Those used for support often have limited, timebound access via privileged session tooling.
- For temporary contractors or short-term vendors (e.g., vendor trials on <=90 days), we can provide an attestation letter. Please confirm if you need those attestation letters included in the evidence bundle.
- Regarding cross-border routing: the roster includes a column 'egress_locations' — Jordan, can you confirm that the EU tenant routing policy is enforced for customers that requested EU-only residency? If not, we'll document the current limitations.

Deliverables we'll provide by Mon EOD (28 Jul):
- CSV roster with columns: name, role, egress_locations, access_level, added_on, contract_term
- Marked-up DPA clause for telemetry/logging processors (dpa_redline_draft.docx)
- Transition plan skeleton for LogStreamer (internal infra note)

Samir — if you want the attestation letters, reply to this thread and Kim (Legal Ops contact) can coordinate signatures.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: dpa_redline_draft.docx (redline), roster_20260725.csv (export), dataflow_20260725.png (diagram)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datapulse.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@datapulse.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessors inventory + transition plan (audit)

Ben / Kim —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts — we received the CSV and the DPA redline. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance reviewers: 

1) EdgeLogix -> LogStreamer change: can you confirm whether EU tenant telemetry destined for LogStreamer ever traverses US-based hops or is routed within EU endpoints only? Our legal team will require a routing statement for tenants who selected EU-only processing.

2) For attestation letters: yes, please include attestation for any temporary contractors that had access in the last 12 months. We need the signatory, title, and effective dates.

Finally, can we do a 20-minute walkthrough Thu 11:00 PT to let our compliance folks ask clarifying questions? If that works I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Samir
--
Samir Patel
Vendor Risk Manager, DataPulse
samir.patel@datapulse.com
